mapName: A Learnable Israel / West Bank - Regionguessing

metas.name: Acre Lamps
metas.note:
These lamps, shaped similarly to Barad Dûr, are unique to Acre. It can be found in several different colours.

NOTE: Similar looking lamps can be found around central Israel, however the gap between the two horns on top of the lamp should confirm Acre.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Architecture
metas.note: Architecture tends to consist of bright and warm-coloured stone buildings, often with a blocky appearance. While Mediterranean-style houses with orange tiled roofs are more common than in other Middle Eastern countries, flat roofs are still just as common.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Area Codes
metas.note: Here is a map of area codes in Israel and the West Bank. Note that only the phone codes featured on the map are regional.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Ashdod Fences
metas.note: This style of blue and white fence is very common to see in Ashdod.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Beit She'an Irrigation Canals
metas.note: You can find these small irrigation canals on the side of the road, in the area around the city of Beit She’an.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Bethlehem House Numbers
metas.note: Blue house numbers with the number written with Arabic numerals in the top left and with Eastern Arabic numerals in the bottom right, with a thin diagonal line between them, can be found in Bethlehem. Street signs will generally have the same format.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Black and White Pole Paint
metas.note: Utility poles commonly feature these painted black and white striped bottoms.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Bnei Brak
metas.note: Bnei Brak is the most Jewish city in Israel, so it is really easy to tell only by looking at the people around. There will usually be people who wear Jewish religious clothes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Cement Rock Walls
metas.note: Rock walls put together with cement are found in the north of Israel.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Chevrons
metas.note: Chevrons are white on black.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Citroën Follow Car
metas.note:
This larger white Citroën follow car with a West Bank licence plate can be found in a region surrounding Jerusalem. It is noticeably found in the cities of Bethlehem and Ramallah.

NOTE: The side of this car features the text “SECURITY” in a bold font. Furthermore, this coverage will always feature a black Street View car with no antenna.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Dead Sea
metas.note:
The Dead Sea can easily be recognised by the dryness surrounding it.

NOTE: It is also visible from Jordan and the West Bank.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Eilat Mountains
metas.note: These tall, rocky mountains can be found east of Eilat, making the city very easy to recognize.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Eilat Pole Paint
metas.note: Poles with blue and white paint on the bottom are unique to Eilat.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Ford Follow Car
metas.note: Another follow car is a small dark blue Ford, which is found in the northwest.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Guardrails
metas.note:
Both A-type and B-type guardrails are common.

NOTE: The only other Middle Eastern country where B-type guardrails are common is Turkey.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Hasolelim Water Reservoir
metas.note: North of the Hasolelim forest reserve you can see this large reservoir.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Hebrew Language
metas.note: You will typically find two languages; Hebrew, which is practically only found in Israel and the West Bank, and Arabic, which is particularly common in the West Bank.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Herzliyah House Numbers
metas.note: Blue, shield-shaped house numbers are unique to the city of Herzliya.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Industrial Chimneys
metas.note: These tall industrial chimneys, by the coast north of Netanya, are visible from far away.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Jericho Vibe
metas.note: Jericho can commonly be recognised by the date palms in a somewhat sparsely built and poor-looking urban setting.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Jerusalem Signs
metas.note: These white rectangular signs with a thin blue border are typically found in Jerusalem.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Jerusalem Stone
metas.note:
In Jerusalem and surrounding cities in the West Bank, nearly every building is built with the same type of material, called Jerusalem stone. Beware that the stone will look much smoother on newer buildings.

NOTE: Single houses with the same material can be found in other towns and cities.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Jerusalem Vibe
metas.note: Most of the West Bank has a semi-arid Mediterranean landscape. It is generally greener than southern Israel, drier than northern Israel and west of Jerusalem, and hillier and less agricultural than central Israel.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Kilometre Markers
metas.note: Kilometre markers are white with a thick border, which can either be red, green or blue.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Mosaic Brick Work
metas.note: This grey mosaic brick work shaped like towers is unique to the city of Harish.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Mount Carmel
metas.note:
Mount Carmel is a long mountain ridge, going northwest to southeast, near the city of Haifa. From the northeast, it can easily be recognised by its direction and size.

There is also a lot of coverage on top of the mountain range, which is generally fairly green and looks noticeably high altitude.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Mount Gilboa
metas.note:
Mount Gilboa is a very dry looking mountain, which can be seen from far away and from many angles.

There is some coverage on top of the mountain, which is very green and often with a very good view over the surrounding valleys.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Nahrriya Lamps
metas.note: This white lamp is unique to Nahariya. It has three arms, with round light bulbs on top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: National Trail
metas.note: The Israel National Trail goes through the entire country and has one of the longest trekkers in the world. The trail goes through more or less every landscape present in the country, from the rocky desert in the south to lush forests in the north. Along the trail you may find these markings, which will typically be orange, blue and white, but can also feature other colour schemes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Ness Ziona House Numbers
metas.note: In Ness Ziona, There is an Israeli flag on house numbers.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Netivot Lamps
metas.note: These metal lamps, characterised by one high and one low lamp put together with a very angular look, are unique to Netivot.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Nezer Mountains
metas.note:
This mountain range, in the far north of Israel, can be recognised by its shape, somewhat resembling a camel's back.

As a bonus, if you are in a city and see these mountains to the west, you will be in Kiryat Shmona.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Palm Tree Plantation
metas.note: Date palm plantations can often be seen close to the Jordanian border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Rahat Follow Car
metas.note: This grey Hyundai follow car is unique to Rahat.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Ramallah Water Tanks
metas.note:
In the city of Ramallah you will generally see several black water tanks on most houses.

NOTE: Several other cities in both the West Bank and Israel can have black water tanks. What makes Ramallah stand out is the sheer number of them on most buildings.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Red and White striped Kerbs
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Road 2/Mediterranean Sea
metas.note:
Road 2 can usually be recognised by the Mediterranean sea being visible on the west side of the road.

NOTE: If you see mountains to the east, you will be somewhere between Haifa and Zikhron Yaakov.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Road 90
metas.note:
Road 90 is the longest road in Israel, and can often be recognised by its dryness combined with the general north to south angle.

Be careful, as road 90 can sometimes look quite similar to roads 31 and 40.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Rosh Haayin House Numbers
metas.note: House numbers in Rosh Haayin are blue, with a G-clef in the bottom left corner.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Roundabouts Ra'anana
metas.note: Roundabout signs which are either very thick or attached to a large cube, can be found in the city of Raanana.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Sea Of Galilee
metas.note: Other than the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean Sea, the only major body of water is the Sea of Galilee. It is noticeably more vegetated than the Dead Sea, making it easily recognisable.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Stop Sign
metas.note: Rather than having a word meaning ‘stop’ written on them, stop signs have a hand painted on them
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Tavor Mountain
metas.note: Mount Tavor is located in the Northern District and can be recognised by its soft, round shape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Tel-Aviv Parking
metas.note:
Finding parking in Tel Aviv is notoriously difficult, meaning the side of almost every road will be full of parked cars.

NOTE: If you are confident that you are in Tel Aviv and see available parking spots, you are more likely to be in the north of the city.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Timna National Park
metas.note: Timna National park can be recognised by the complete dryness combined with the mountain ridges in all directions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: White Suzuki Follow Car
metas.note: A significant portion of the coverage in the West Bank has a visible security follow car. The most extensive of these is a small white Suzuki, which is found in the central and southern regions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Yellow Fences Kiryat Motzkin
metas.note: These yellow fences and signposts are unique to Kiryat Motzkin.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.
